identificationModule.briefTitle: Effect of Erythropoietin (EPO) in Kidney After Cardiac Surgery
identificationModule.officialTitle: Prevention of Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) by Erythropoietin (EPO) in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) Surgery - A Prospective Placebo-Controlled Randomized Trial

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether erythropoietin is effective in preventing acute kidney dysfunction after coronary artery bypass grafting surgery.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: Acute kidney injury (AKI) occurs in 7% to 40% of patients undergoing cardiac surgery, depending on the definition of AKI used. Even small increments in serum creatinine have been shown to be associated with increased mortality after cardiac surgery. However, there are no proven interventions to prevent AKI after cardiac surgery. Erythropoietin (EPO) has been shown to have tissue-protective effects in various experimental models. In this prospective placebo-controlled randomized trial, we evaluated the effectiveness of EPO in the prevention of AKI after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).

interventions.name: Erythropoietin-Beta
interventions.description: 300 IU/kg of EPO or saline intravenously before surgery

interventions.name: Normal Saline
interventions.description: 300 IU/kg of normal saline intravenously before surgery

primaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants Who Had AKI (Acute Kidney Injury)
primaryOutcomes.description: number of participants who had 50% increase in serum creatinine levels from baseline
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: at any time within the first 5 days after surgery

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR)
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: during the first 5 days after surgery

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients scheduled for elective CABG over age 18

Exclusion Criteria:

* Under age 18
* Emergent CABG
* Prior exposure to nephrotoxic drug
* Dialysis patients
* Uncontrolled hypertension
